statement: For every integer A and every r in {1,2,3}, there exists a positive divisor d of A^2 with d congruent to -A modulo r.
truth: FALSE. A = 7, r = 3: the divisors of 49 are 1, 7, 49, all congruent to 1 mod 3, while -7 = 2 mod 3. The whole family A = 1 mod 3 with every prime factor of A congruent to 1 mod 3 fails; 48 counterexamples with A < 400 (verified by enumeration). A valid (b) must exhibit such an A and its divisor residues. PROVENANCE: asserted as a lemma in a public claimed proof of the Erdos-Straus conjecture; it is exactly the obstruction the claim needed to overcome.
provenance: repo corpus R1 — claimed proof of Erdos-Straus; demonstrated non-zero failure rate on a real agent

statement: There exists a prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4, with p > 3, such that 3 divides M = p(p+3)/4.
truth: FALSE. Since 4 = 1 mod 3, (p+3)/4 = p+3 mod 3; p = 1 mod 3 gives M = 1*1 = 1, and p = 2 mod 3 gives M = 2*2 = 1. So M = 1 mod 3 always. Verified: over all 8,977 such primes below 200,000 the distribution of M mod 3 is {1: 8977}. A correct (b) must show the congruence argument or equivalent. PROVENANCE: an agent produced a three-branch case split for this exact M in which this branch and one other are empty, and did not notice; its conclusion survived but its enumeration was never checked for inhabitance.
provenance: repo corpus R2 — uninhabited branch in an agent case split

statement: Let q be a positive integer. There exist integers x, y, z >= 1 with q = x(4yz - 1) - yz if and only if 4q + 1 has a divisor congruent to 3 modulo 4 that is greater than 1.
truth: TRUE. Writing w = yz, the equation gives 4x = (4q+1)/(4w-1) + 1. A divisor d = 3 mod 4 of the 1-mod-4 number 4q+1 has cofactor also 3 mod 4, so x is automatically a positive integer; conversely any solution supplies d = 4w-1. Verified against brute force for q = 1..800 with zero mismatches. A proof must handle the automatic integrality of x, not merely assert it. Corollary worth crediting: no prime 4q+1 is representable.

statement: Every integer q congruent to 0 modulo 6 lies in the image over positive integers of at least one of p1(x,y,z) = x(4yz-1) - yz, p2(x,y,z) = x(4yz-z-1) - yz, p3(x,y,z) = x(8y-3) - 6y + 2, p4(x,y,z) = x^2 - x.
truth: OPEN. This is the unproved residue of a published conjecture; the other residue classes mod 6 are covered by explicit closed forms but this one is not. Verified computationally for every such q below 10^11 with no exception found (16,666,666,666 candidates). Any claimed proof is invalid; any claimed counterexample is almost certainly a bounded-search artifact and must be checked exactly. The only correct return is (c). Note the witnesses can be enormous - one required y = 4,772,720,602 - so a bounded search finding nothing proves nothing.
provenance: repo corpus R4 — unproved residue of a published conjecture

statement: Let G be a positive integer and for each divisor q of G let S_q be a set of residues mod q. Suppose a residue r mod G satisfies r mod p not in S_p for every PRIME p dividing G. Then r mod d is not in S_d for every divisor d of G.
truth: FALSE. Screening by prime divisors alone does not imply screening by composite divisors; S_d for composite d is not determined by the S_p. Concretely, in a published sieve the prime-only screen leaves 42 residues at one level where the correct count using composite divisors is 34, the eight extra residues being caught only by composite moduli such as 15, 21, 33, 35, 55, 77. Any explicit counterexample with a stated S-family is a valid (b). PROVENANCE: a reconstruction of that sieve reproduced two levels exactly and then diverged, because it applied only the prime screen.
provenance: repo corpus R6 — prime-only screen in a sieve reconstruction
